paragraphs.source: We handle the Canadian pulse market classes used in food and feed. Lentils: red (small and large) and green (Laird, Richlea, Eston). Peas: yellow and green. Beans: navy, pinto, black, and kidney. Specialty classes only when named on the offer. Availability follows the crop year.

Ask for a current specification sheet and sample. Typical parameters follow Canadian Grain Commission dry-grade moisture unless the contract is tighter: red lentils 13% max, green lentils 14% max, peas 16% max, dry beans commonly 14–16% in trade. Grade, size, colour, foreign material, splits, damaged seed, and protein are set on the recap. Purity figures such as 99% are a contract spec, not a CGC grade name.
Lentils
Canada is the world’s leading lentil exporter. We offer the classes that dominate global trade, prepared whole or split.
Red lentils

Canadian lentils are graded in two CGC classes: Red, and lentils other than red. Red is the class most often requested. Small red is the volume class. Large red is offered when the crop year produces it. Formats: whole red, dehulled whole (football), and split red (masoor dal). CGC dry moisture for red lentils is below 13.1% — contracts usually write 13% max. Tighter limits are named on the recap. We are open to shipping whole red and masoor dal to India, Bangladesh, Turkey, Mersin, UAE, Iraq, Algeria, Sudan, Egypt, Pakistan, and other destinations. Colour, moisture, and a clean split are graded to the contract.
Green lentils

Green lentils sit in the CGC class lentils other than red. Trade names are Laird (large), Richlea (medium), and Eston (small). Colour, stain, and damage decide the grade. CGC dry moisture is below 14.1% — contracts usually write 14% max. Variety names such as CDC lines change by crop year; the offer states the market class, not a seed catalogue.
Other classes
French-type / dark speckled, extra-small reds, and other specialty lots when the crop and demand line up. Inquire by crop year.
Formats: whole · dehulled · split · flour (on request)
Peas

Canada is the world’s largest pea producer and exporter. Yellow peas dominate export volumes; green peas serve food and specialty channels. Both are used in food, splitting, milling, protein extraction, and feed.
Yellow peas
Yellow peas: the volume class. Colour, size, and bleach or stain are the commercial controls. Whole, split, feed, or milling. Moisture as above unless the recap is tighter.
Green peas
Smaller market, tighter colour specification. Used in food packing, splitting, and some ingredient applications. Colour and bleaching are inspected closely.
Other pea types
Maple and specialty peas when available. Feed peas for livestock, pet food, and aquaculture programs.
Formats: whole · split · feed · flour / milling stock (on request)
Dry beans
Canada produces a wide range of dry edible beans for domestic canning and export. Classes and growing regions differ from peas and lentils; we source to the class you specify.

paragraphs.source: SUSTAINABILITY
Lead

Pulse crops fix nitrogen, break cereal disease cycles, and use water efficiently relative to many other proteins. That is not a marketing line. That is why the farms in our organization keep them in the rotation, and why food companies and the global pulse trade treat them as a staple protein — not a novelty ingredient.
On the farm

Lentils, peas, and beans reduce synthetic nitrogen demand in the following crop. The farmers we work with in Alberta, Saskatchewan, Manitoba, and Ontario grow them inside Canadian cropping systems that have spent two decades cutting tillage and improving soil cover. Quality at destination starts with how those farms are run.
In the product
paragraphs.status: Review: heading, instruction, split copy, or wording difference

paragraphs.source: Pulses are high in protein and fibre and low in fat. They are a practical ingredient for plant-based foods, traditional staple diets, and feed rations that need a Canadian-origin protein source.
In our operation
We aim to move grain the shortest practical distance from farm to plant to port.
Cleaning recovers a higher share of a lot as food-grade product instead of discounting it.
By-products from processing are directed to feed where food-grade use is not possible.
We will report on energy, waste, and sourcing as those measurements become part of customer requirements.

9. FAQ
paragraphs.status: Review: heading, instruction, split copy, or wording difference

paragraphs.source: Do you sell only in bulk, or can you pack retail bags?
paragraphs.status: Review: heading, instruction, split copy, or wording difference

paragraphs.source: We supply bulk quantities, bulk-bag totes, and smaller lots in client-specific bags. Optional branding is available to suit the buyer and the destination market. Artwork and bag specs are agreed before packing.
Can you send a sample before we contract?
Yes. We send representative samples of the offered lot or of current-crop quality. A sample is a guide, not a substitute for the contract specification.
What is the minimum order?
[State your real MOQ — e.g. one 20' container, one tote trial, or a metric-tonne minimum.] Trial quantities can be discussed for first-time buyers.

paragraphs.source: Can a third-party inspector attend?

Yes, when the contract names the agency and who pays. Inspection is booked against the packed lot, not a display sample. Under GPC Pulses Contract No. 1, an official or independent inspector certificate is typically final as to shipped quality unless the recap says otherwise. Organic lots only from certified supply.
Which export documents do you provide?

As specified in the contract: commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading, certificate of origin (including CUSMA origin certification where the cargo is wholly obtained in Canada and the importer claims preference), CFIA phytosanitary certificate, fumigation certificate where the destination requires it, and CGC or other grade and weight certificates. Residue or quality analysis by agreement. A CBSA export declaration is filed for commercial shipments leaving Canada for destinations other than the United States.
How do you price and how is payment handled?

Offers are based on current origin values, grade, packing, freight, and currency. Quoted in USD unless another currency is agreed. Validity is stated on the recap. The contract form is named on the recap — GPC Pulses Contract No. 1 or another agreed form. Payment is by letter of credit, telegraphic transfer, or another instrument named in the contract. Terms are written before the cargo moves.
What contract form do you use?

The recap names the form. We work on GPC Pulses Contract No. 1 — the standard contract of the Global Pulse Confederation — or on another form both parties accept. Quality, weight, documents, force majeure, and dispute resolution follow that form. Program pricing is a separate commercial discussion: volume, shipment calendar, and basis risk must be defined.
